A DIFFERENT KIND OF PLAYER

Small cells. Moving pictures.

Celluloid samples each video frame, scales it down, and maps its pixels to a color palette. Every square you see represents one spreadsheet cell.

  1. Pick your source. Drop a video or enable your webcam. The sample animation is ready to explore.
  2. Find your look. Choose a grid, color palette, and frame rate. Apply settings to reconvert the source.
  3. Make it a spreadsheet. Export an .ods file. In desktop LibreOffice, allow macros for your trusted export, then use Tools → Macros → Run Macro → this document → Standard → Playback → PlayVideo.
  4. Go live in Calc. Run the local companion and connect it to stream uploaded video or live webcam frames into actual cells.

The exported file contains real cell colors and animation code. LibreOffice playback speed depends on your computer and grid size. Audio is not included.

THE REAL SPREADSHEET EXPERIENCE

Let Calc be the screen.

The local companion opens a fresh LibreOffice spreadsheet and changes its cell colors as your video or webcam plays.

  1. Download the toolkit and extract it. The included setup launcher installs LibreOffice and checks its Python connection.
  2. From the extracted folder, run: 
    Linux / macOS:  bash setup.sh
Windows:        .\setup.cmd
    It prints a local URL and a temporary pairing token. Open that URL for the most reliable camera and Calc connection.
  3. Paste the token below, connect, then press Play or start your webcam.

When using the hosted app, the companion also needs --allow-origin with this site's origin. Your browser may require local network permission; opening the companion's local URL avoids this restriction.

Not connected. No spreadsheet is being controlled.

// THE TERMINAL ROUTE

same cells. no browser.

The CLI handles files or a live camera directly. Install FFmpeg and a matching LibreOffice + Python UNO installation, then run from the repository root. 

# video → portable indexed frames
python3 -m native.cli convert clip.mp4 -o clip.celluloid.json

# video → actual Calc cells
python3 -m native.cli play clip.mp4 --width 48 --palette grayscale --hold

# live camera → actual Calc cells (Linux)
python3 -m native.cli webcam --device /dev/video0

For macOS, use --device 0:none. On Windows, use the camera’s DirectShow name, such as --device "Integrated Camera". Hardware capture settings depend on your device.

The application needs no web GUI. Calc still opens a window to display the cells. Use --headless --save final.ods for scripted file processing. Press Ctrl+C to stop streaming.
